title: After South Africa Tour Snub, Shreyanka Patil Earns India A Call for England Series
excerpt: Overlooked for the senior tour of South Africa, off-spinning all-rounder Shreyanka Patil has been named in all three India A squads for the home series against England A starting November 30 in Pune, with Kashvee Gautam also returning from knee surgery.
body:
• Shreyanka Patil has been picked in India A squads for all three formats of the home series against England A, starting November 30 in Pune and Mumbai.
  • Patil last played an international in India's victorious Asian Games campaign, and was overlooked for the home series against Zimbabwe and the upcoming senior tour of South Africa.
  • She is one of five players named in all three formats, alongside Minnu Mani, Shipra Giri, Tanisha Singh and Saima Thakor.
  • Fast-bowling all-rounder Kashvee Gautam returns in the white-ball squads after knee surgery, having made her comeback in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy for Chandigarh.

Shreyanka Patil has been named in the India A squads for the all-format home series against England A, days after being left out of the senior squad for the tour of South Africa. The series is to be held in Pune and Mumbai from November 30, Cricbuzz reported.

Patil, an off-spinning all-rounder, last played an international game in India's victorious Asian Games campaign, before being overlooked for the home series against Zimbabwe and the upcoming tour of South Africa. For the senior T20I squad, ESPNcricinfo reported, the spin options of Deepti Sharma, Shree Charani and Prema Rawat left no place for her. The India A selection gives her an immediate route to press her case in all three formats.

Five Players Across Every Format

Patil is one of five players included in the squads for each of the three formats, alongside Minnu Mani, Shipra Giri, Tanisha Singh and Saima Thakor, according to Cricbuzz. India A will be led by batter Anushka Sharma in the three T20s and three one-day matches, with Minnu Mani as her deputy. Mani then captains the multi-day game, with Tejal Hasabnis as vice-captain.

Kashvee Gautam's return is the other notable selection. The fast-bowling all-rounder, who last featured during India's T20I tour of South Africa in April, was sidelined by a knee injury that required surgery. She made her comeback in the ongoing Senior Women's T20 Trophy for Chandigarh and is included in the white-ball squads.

The Schedule

The series begins on November 30 with the T20 leg in Pune: the first game starts at 1 p.m., and the second and third T20s, on December 3 and 5, start at 6 p.m. Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium hosts the three one-day matches on December 8, 11 and 14, the first of them a day game starting at 9 a.m. The Wankhede also hosts the multi-day fixture from December 19.

The T20 squad in full: Anushka Sharma (captain), Minnu Mani (vice-captain), Vrinda Dinesh, Tanisha Singh, Sanika Chalke, Niki Prasad, G Kamalini, Shipra Giri, Amanjot Kaur, Shreyanka Patil, Vaishnavi Sharma, Prema Rawat, Saima Thakor, Monica Patel and Kashvee Gautam.

For Patil, the assignment is clear. The selectors have not closed the door — they have sent her to the level immediately below the senior side, in every format, against an England A team at home. Performances there, starting November 30, are her argument for the next senior squad.
